claim: No. 1 on the chart dated January 3, 1970: Raindrops Keep Fallin' On My Head, B.J. Thomas (first 70s chart)
No. 1 on January 4, 1975: Lucy In The Sky With Diamonds, Elton John, start of the 1975 one-week run sequence
No. 1 on July 3, 1976: Silly Love Songs, Wings, weeks at No. 1 = 5 (fifth and final week)
No. 1 on December 29, 1979: Escape (The Pina Colada Song), Rupert Holmes (last 70s chart)
You Light Up My Life, Debby Boone, reaches No. 1 on October 15, 1977 (linked in body)
Song of the Year, 20th Grammys: two winners, Love Theme From A Star Is Born (Evergreen) (Streisand, Paul Williams) and You Light Up My Life (Joe Brooks)

Hot 100 published since August 1958; 1970 compiled from retail sales surveys and radio playlists; 21 different No. 1s in 1970; Raindrops first No. 1 for Thomas, from Butch Cassidy soundtrack, four weeks

35 different No. 1s in 1975; after Lucy in the Sky (Jan 4, 11) the next 12 chart-toppers each spent one week at No. 1, the longest run of consecutive single-week No. 1s in Hot 100 history to that point; ended by Philadelphia Freedom April 12
1970s Hot 100 based on weekly physical sales and radio airplay; decade list of No. 1 singles
Written by Joseph Brooks; Boone's version No. 1 ten consecutive weeks in 1977; earned Brooks a Grammy for Song of the Year and an Academy Award for Best Original Song
